lots.title: Provision of Minor Disability Adaptations (Minor Building Works) in Privately Owned Properties
lots.description: Installation of equipment and minor works at properties for people with disabilities under the London Borough of Bexley's Building Services Framework 6278 (Lot 11). Works are electronically awarded via a Works Approval Form per job, priced from an agreed pricing schedule, and are typically carried out in occupied, privately owned residential premises used by vulnerable clients. Majority of work is VAT exempt. Initial term 1 Nov 2026 - 31 Oct 2028, with two one-year extension options at the Council's discretion (document title references an overall window of 1 Nov 2026 - 31 Oct 2030).
requirements: All work electronically awarded via a Council-issued Works Approval Form indicating cost, scope, and job code (A/B/C/D); contractor must send prompt electronic acknowledgement.
Pricing for works and materials is taken from the agreed Pricing Schedule; any additions/variations must be agreed by the Authorised Officer before commencement.

Response times: Code A (hospital discharge) within 24 hours; Code B (emergency) within 48 hours; Code C (urgent) within 5 working days; Code D (standard) within 15 working days from the date of the Works Approval Form.
Financial penalties of up to £100 per day may apply for late Code A (hospital discharge) works.
All work compliant with JCT MTC 2024 Terms and Conditions, plus the specified time frames and penalty clause.

Contractor submits an 'Application for Payment' prior to invoicing for reconciliation; monthly electronic invoicing; invoices must be submitted within six months of the Works Approval Form; Council pays within 30 days of agreed invoice.
Optional early-payment (dynamic discount) Programme offered via Oxygen Finance; participation voluntary.
Majority of works are VAT exempt; VAT to be shown separately as a net extra when applicable.
All operatives visiting clients must hold a current enhanced DBS check; contractor maintains a staff list and keeps checks up to date.
TUPE (Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006) applies to staff of incumbent contractors.
No smoking permitted in client premises; operatives must not use client phone, WC, kitchen, electricity/gas/water without permission; no sound equipment.
Works must comply with all Acts of Parliament, Byelaws, local authority and statutory undertaker requirements; contractor pays all statutory fees.

Works must comply with current Building Regulations; notices to Building Control forwarded to Authorised Officer; Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 and BS 7671:2008 IET Wiring Regulations 18th Edition apply.
Contractor is responsible for making good damage to building, services, roads, footpaths, landscaping, and finished surfaces caused by the works at their own expense.
Before work, contractor independently verifies location of underground services, wires, cables and overhead wires; pays all disconnection/reconnection costs.
Contractor must protect contents, chattels and personal belongings of occupiers; provide dust sheets, tarpaulins, timbering, boarding, polythene sheeting; ladders padded to avoid damage.
No spirits or chemicals without prior written consent of Authorised Officer; no explosives; works to minimise noise, dust, nuisance.
Access arranged directly with client by prior appointment; contractor must not arrive unannounced; 'calling card/abortive visit card' left if no access.
Clients are vulnerable; operatives must show proof of identity, treat clients with courtesy, respect cultural needs, and maintain confidentiality.
Client must not be left without WC, cooker, heating or electricity at end of day; adequate temporary services provided if unavoidable.

All items/products installed per manufacturer's instructions with all components supplied; no second-hand materials; fixings sized/typed to suit building fabric; equipment must withstand client's weight and be fit for purpose.

Electrical works: isolate/disconnect/make safe circuits before work; chase walls to bury services; uPVC surface trunking on solid concrete walls/ceilings; all electrical work per BS 7671:2008 18th Edition; electrical installation certificate compliant with Part P provided on completion for all new circuits.

Staff suitability: all staff must have necessary training, qualifications and current registration (e.g. Gas Safe for gas works; Registered Competent Persons or Registered Third-Party Certifiers for electrical works); staff registered under CSCS or equivalent.
Trainees/apprentices must be accompanied at all times by a fully qualified person; Authorised Officer may request evidence of qualifications/trade association registration.
All staff must wear visible photographic identification cards (valid for max 1 year) containing photograph, name, trade, contractor name/address, contact telephone, expiry date.

Waste disposal: waste carted away daily by the contractor to a licensed tip; contractor provides waste carrier/broker registration; compliance with Environmental Protection Act 1990; Waste Disposal Certificates retained and available on request; recycling encouraged.
Spillages: contractor provides a process and 'spill kits' on vehicles; disposal sites (normal and hazardous) disclosed; all spillages reported to Authorised Officer.

Health and Safety: contractor registered with an SSIP Forum member (e.g. CHAS, EXOR Health & Safety, OHSAS 18001) for the duration of the contract; nominated H&S responsible person; compliance with Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

Asbestos: comply with Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 (CAR 2012); do not use asbestos-containing materials; survey premises before work; cease work and notify Authorised Officer if asbestos found/suspected; only specialist contractors appointed by the Council may remove asbestos.

Glazing: full compliance with Approved Document K (Building Regulations) and Regulation 14 of the Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992; safety/toughened glass marked per BS EN 12600; glass per BS 952-1:1995 Parts 1 & 2 and BS 6262-4:2018.
Portable electrical equipment: maximum 110V; double-insulated or effectively earthed; compliant with Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998.
Hot works require safe working method statements, generic risk assessments, notification to Authorised Officer and a Permit to Work; operatives experienced and trained.
Working at height: compliance with Working at Height Regulations 2005; safe working method statements and risk assessments provided; scaffolding per Council's scaffolding protocol.
Hazardous substances: not used without written COSHH assessment on Premises; compliance with COSHH 2002.
PPE: compliant with Personal Protective Equipment at Work (Amendment) Regulations 2022; eye protection to BS EN ISO 16321 (2022); hearing and respiratory protection in noisy/dusty areas.

Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (CDM 2015): where applicable, contractor notifies the Council, plans/manages/monitors the construction phase, and the Principal Contractor role is deemed included in the Pricing Schedule (no additional cost).
Accidents/incidents reported immediately to the Authorised Officer and to HSE under RIDDOR 2013 where applicable; HSE Improvement/Prohibition Notices forwarded to Authorised Officer.
Quotation visits: contractor visits sites free of charge when requested prior to approval.
Pricing: when requested, prices must be fully inclusive of all work to complete the specified adaptation (including call out, site clearance, waste disposal).

Warranties: defects/breakdowns occurring within 12 months of repair or installation rectified by contractor at no extra cost (except spare parts); faults rectified within 14 days of notice; failure to complete satisfactorily, or 10+ default notices in 12 months, may trigger re-procurement with costs deducted from contractor; parts replaced free and re-warranted for 12 months; contractor completes warranty cards with the client.
Additional work beyond the grant approval must be reported with an estimate to the grants team before commencing.
Confidentiality: strict confidentiality of client identity and contact details; compliance with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act.

Communication: contractor maintains active means of contact (answerphone not acceptable during normal hours); supervisors equipped with mobile phones; contractor leaves return time/date and contact number with client during interruptions.

Performance review meetings with the Authorised Officer covering customer satisfaction, response times, financial monitoring, invoice queries, abortive calls, quality of work, H&S, DBS declarations, and audit of contractor reports; frequency set by the Authorised Officer.
